chunks: From him, from ʿAlī, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Qutaybah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If you have prayed behind an Imam whom you approve of in a salat in which the recitation is said aloud, and you do not hear his recitation, then recite for yourself. But if you can hear the murmuring, then do not recite.
Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام
about praying behind one whom I approve of: should I recite behind him? He said: Behind one whom you approve of, do not recite behind him.

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual salat being performed in congregation
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the recitation of the Qur'an within salat
key_terms.الْهَمْهَمَةَ: the low murmur or subdued sound of the Imam’s recitation
key_terms.تَرْتَضِي: to deem acceptable or be satisfied with as one worthy of following
key_terms.تُجْهَرُ: is recited aloud in an audible prayer

ai.seo_question: Should a person recite al-Fatihah behind an Imam in audible prayer if he cannot hear the recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of recitation while praying behind an Imam whom one deems acceptable. It indicates that in audible prayers, if the follower does not hear the Imam’s recitation at all, he may recite for himself, but if he hears even the Imam’s low murmur, he should not recite.
